newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude grades firm on products, North Sea.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude grades firm on products, North Sea.

text.p: Differentials paid for U.S. domestic grades continued to firm Thursday in line with stronger products prices in the U.S. Gulf and bullish North Sea loading programs, traders said.
Outright September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing benchmark stood some 10 cents higher at $20.25-35 a barrel, with the September/October spread at minus 18-20 cents.
"The Brent-WTI coming in sharply, and the North Sea crude programs drove the grades higher," said a dealer.
September Brent-WTI was at a $1.15, and October $1.24.
In London, an August 28-30 Brent cargo was sold to a Wall Street trader for September Brent minus five cents, seven cents stronger than the previous deal.

On the loading front, Norway's Gullfaks crude system will load 10 standard 855,000 barrels cargoes in September, down sharply from the 19 due in August. Statfjord scheduled loadings for September were set at 24 cargoes, four less than the original August frame.
Domestic grades saw Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sell out to 25-27 cents over the September WTI, around eight cents stronger than Wednesday.
Midland/WTI sold at a 30 and 29 cents discount to WTI, and Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire at -32 cents.

West Texas Sour/Midland was pegged at $1.35 and $1.32 under WTI, the last deals confirmed. Stronger sour prices have also been seen in October, despite the expected flow of Iraqi crude exports to the U.S. Gulf within the next six weeks.
Postings Plus for September moved at $1.87 and $1.90. slightly stronger than deals yesterday at $1.86 and $1.87.
